# The Midnight Sun's Promise

## Scripture
"From the rising of the sun to the place where it sets, the name of the LORD is to be praised." — Psalm 113:3

## Reflection
Summer nights in the far north hold a strange, beautiful secret: the sun barely dips below the horizon before rising again. The sky never fully darkens—just a long, lavender twilight that whispers of dawn even at midnight.

This "midnight sun" reminds me of how God's faithfulness works in our lives. Even in our darkest seasons, there is always a glimmer of His light. The sun doesn't truly abandon the northern skies; it merely hides for a few hours, promising to return. Likewise, God's presence never fully leaves us—even when we can't see it, even when the shadows feel long.

Psalm 113 reminds us that praise belongs to God "from the rising of the sun to the place where it sets." But I wonder—what about the hours in between? Perhaps the midnight sun teaches us that God's praise isn't confined to our bright, easy moments. He is just as worthy of worship in the twilight of uncertainty, in the gray hours of waiting, in the seasons that feel suspended between endings and beginnings.

The same God who holds the sun in its orbit holds you too. His light is not diminished by your circumstances. It may look different—softer, subtler—but it has never stopped shining.

## Prayer
Father of Lights, thank You that Your presence never dims, even when my sky feels dark. Teach me to praise You in every season—bright or twilight. Help me trust that Your dawn is always coming. Amen.
